problem.description: During the March window, two separately-approved changes ran in overlapping windows: one on the legacy-billing-api service and one on the legacy-billing-db it relied on. Individually each was low risk; together the API was mid-deploy while its database was being failed over, and the billing service went dark for 40 minutes. A second incident the same night took down a checkout path because two changes hit BOTH load-balancers fronting it at once, so its redundancy was gone. Lesson recorded by the CAB: a change is not safe in isolation -- before approving a window, cross-check each change against everything every other concurrent change relies on to run -- the hosts it runs on, the databases and queues it uses, and the services beneath it -- including shared and indirect dependencies, not just the same configuration item.
problem.short_description: Post-incident review: concurrent changes on dependent systems caused a service outage
